english: Earth, the mother, was carrying (bearing) a son. He is born. He has awareness (is alert), and he is awake. He grew big and drank broth. His hands grew. Then he stood up and seized a new spear. She was trembling. She said to him: 'What are you seeking?' He said: 'I am seeking the snake who covers/hides the streams.' Then he went to that snake, and she caught sight of him, and she was trembling. Then he was overcoming her, and she vanished (was lost). O Sky, O Father, your son is great.
uncertain: dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr: both NOM; read as apposition 'Earth the mother'; could also be a verbless 'Earth is mother' but bʰéret needs a subject.
ǵeǵónh₁e: PRF 'is born / has been born' (state), not a narrative past.
bʰebʰówdʰe só-kʷe bʰéwdʰeti: PRF 'has awareness' then PRS 'is awake' (or SBJV of bʰewdʰ- 'will wake'); present tense inside a past narrative is odd.
séh₂ trémt / séh₂ tósmey mléwHt: 'she' taken as the mother (only female so far); no noun given.
h₁yéh₂: relative fem NOM.SG (snake as subject of ḱéleti) or neut NOM/ACC.PL agreeing with sréwmn̥h₂ ('the streams which [it] hides'); chose fem NOM.SG since the snake is fem (tā́m).
ḱéleti: 'covers, hides' (PRS) or SBJV of ḱel- 'will conceal'.
séh₂-kʷe tóm kʷéḱt séh₂-kʷe tréset: séh₂ could be the snake or the mother; read as the snake (nearest fem noun).
térh₂ut: PST 'was overcoming', not AOR 'overcame'.
néḱt: 'vanished, was lost', not explicitly 'died'.
dyéw ph₂tér: VOC (or LOC) — an address 'O Sky Father, your son…'; text does not say the son is Sky Father's son in 3rd person, and the mother here is Earth.

english: A horse was dwelling (settling) by the stream, and a wolf came to it. It (the horse) said to a man: 'Make that wolf disappear (kill it)!' He (the man) said: 'If you carry me, I will make it disappear.' Then it (the horse) was carrying him, and he struck it (the wolf) with a spit/spear. Then the wolf fell and grew cold. Then the horse said to him: 'Let me go!' The man did not let it go, and he was yoking it to a wheel (chariot). Now the horse pulls his wheel. Whoever carries a man, the man drives him.
uncertain: tḱéyt: PST of tḱey- 'settle / dwell' (also 'cultivate'); read 'was dwelling'.
gʷémt tóm: 'stepped/came to it' — ACC as goal; no hostile verb.
só wiHrṓy wérh₁t: só not named; read as the horse (only prior NOM besides wolf).
noḱéye / noḱéyōh₂: gloss 'make disappear, cause death'; rendered as kill.
gʷréwh₁: INS of gʷéru 'spit, skewer' / 'spear'.
kʷékʷlōy / kʷékʷlom: 'wheel' (DAT/ACC); chariot/cart presumably intended.
yunégt: PST 'was yoking', not AOR.
déwkti / h₂éǵeti: PRS gnomic; h₂éǵeti could also be SBJV of h₂eǵ- 'say' (reading 'drives' chosen).

english: A man fell in the fight. His horses were standing, and they did not drink. Then they lay down. Then his twin said to them: 'Swift horses, (you two) stand up! He is gone, and I will drive you on.' They did not stand up. They are mindful of him (remember him). Then Father Sky was looking at them and said to them: 'Horses, do not lie down! His fame is imperishable.' Then they stood up and were pulling that wheel (chariot) away from that fight.
uncertain: sth₂tóm: AOR/IMP 2DU 'you two stand up' addressed to plural VOC h₁éḱwōs — number mismatch; alternatively adjective sth₂tóm 'standing' ACC/NOM.SG, which does not fit.
tósyo yemHós: 'his twin' — whose twin is the fallen man's (non-reflexive tósyo).
lelóykʷe: PRF 'is gone / has left' (not explicitly 'is dead').
usmé-kʷe ǵʰéyoh₂: usmé ACC.PL 'you (pl.)'; ǵʰéyoh₂ SBJV 1SG 'I will/let me drive on'.
memnḗr: PRF 3PL 'they are mindful of / remember' (state).
kh₃téwi / kh₃téws: 'fight' LOC/ABL; battle presumably intended.
kʷékʷlom: 'wheel'; chariot presumably intended.
duként: PST 'were pulling', not AOR.

english: Then the sheep said to the horses (variant: to the horse): 'The heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses.'
uncertain: owis, eḱwobʰ(y)os, eḱwomos, agʰnutoi, eḱwōns, aǵontm̥, nerm̥, widn̥tei: not in lexicon/analyzer (older Schleicher-style orthography, no laryngeals); read from knowledge, not tool-verified.
eḱwobʰ(y)os (eḱwomos): two alternative DAT.PL endings printed in parentheses — the text gives variants, not one form.
ḱēr: analyzer gives only LEMMA 'heart'; read as NOM subject of agʰnutoi.
agʰnutoi: read as MID PRS 3SG 'is pained / grieves'.
moi: GEN/DAT.SG enclitic 1st person; read DAT 'me', with widn̥tei DAT.SG participle 'to me seeing'.
aǵontm̥: ACC.SG participle 'driving' agreeing with nerm̥ 'man'.

english: A dog was lying in the enclosure of the cattle. The cattle came to that enclosure from the field (pasture). Then it (the dog) stood up and drove them out of that enclosure. They were saying to it: 'What (why), dog, do you eat in it?' It said: 'I do not eat in it, and in it we two lie.' They were looking at it. Then the cattle grew tired, and a man came and drove it (the dog) out of that enclosure. He who does not eat in the enclosure, let him not lie in it.
uncertain: ḱéywosdʰh₂: MID PRS 1DU 'we two lie' — in the dog's own first-person singular speech; presumably 1SG 'I lie' intended.
kʷíd: NOM/ACC 'what' (could be 'why'); 'what do you eat in it' vs 'why do you eat'.
tósmi: LOC m/n 'in it/that'; refers back to the enclosure.
tóns: masc ACC.PL for gʷówes (cattle).
tóm (in 'tóm-kʷe tósmead gʰórtōd h₁élh₂t'): read as the dog; could grammatically be any masc singular.
mē ḱéyih₁to: prohibitive with MID OPT 'may he not lie'.

english: Fire (Agni) ran away from the place of sacrifice (bowing/distribution), and was hiding (himself) in the waters, and the large fish grew warm. They became restless, and they were swimming (or: caught/obtained). Men were seeking him, and did not find him. Then a large fish said to them: 'Agni lies in the river.' Then they were seeing him. He (Agni) said to that fish: 'Fish, they will (shall) kill you.' Then he went to that place of sacrifice, and they were sacrificing to him. Now he licks that place of sacrifice (offering). Now they strike the fish and cook them in the fire. Agni is the guest of men. 'Agni, giver of good things, do not leave us!' May he burn in that place of sacrifice.
uncertain: némesos: GEN/ABL of némos; read ABL 'from'. Analyzer also offers a separate noun némesos 'act of distributing' NOM.SG, which would make it a second subject.
némos/némesi: gloss 'bowing, bending; sacrifice, worship; place of sacrifice, clearing' — 'grove/sanctuary' presumably intended; 'he licks that némos' then = the offering or the place.
ḱéleto: MID PST 'was hiding (himself)'.
skʷálōs / skʷálos: 'large fish'.
sn̥h₂ént: AOR of senh₂- 'obtained, caught' or PST of sneh₂- 'were swimming'; chose swimming (fish subject).
widónt / widéh₁yont: AOR 'found, saw' then PST 'were seeing'.
moréyōnti: SBJV 3PL — future 'will kill' or exhortative 'let them kill'; curse reading.
tód némos gʷéh₂t: ACC goal 'went to'.
h₁yáǵyont + DAT tósmey: 'were sacrificing to / worshipping him'.
léyǵʰti / gʷʰn̥sḱónti / pékʷonti: PRS (aetiological 'now').
mē linékʷs: prohibitive with PST (injunctive) 2SG; fine as 'do not leave'.
dʰégʷʰoyh₁t: OPT 'may he burn'.

english: Dawn grew bright, and the man woke up. He stood up and was clothing himself with bronze (copper). He put on (footwear). He grasped a spit/spear and a bow, and was stretching that bow. Then he was yoking swift horses to the wheel (chariot). His brother was standing on that wheel, and he was driving them. He said to his father: 'Father, I am going to the fight. Be mindful of me (remember me).' The father said: 'May Father Sky protect you, and may you win great fame.'
uncertain: h₂éyesh₁: INS of h₂éyos 'metal, copper, bronze'.
h₂uHtó: MID AOR 'put on (footwear)' with no object.
gʷéru: 'spit, skewer' / 'spear'.
tn̥néwt / yunégt / h₂éǵet: PST 'was stretching/yoking/driving', not AOR.
kʷékʷlōy / kʷékʷloy: 'wheel' DAT/LOC; chariot presumably intended.
tósyo bʰréh₂tēr: 'his brother' = the man's brother.
só tósyo ph₂tréy wéwket: só could be the man or the brother; tósyo (non-reflexive) strictly suggests the father of someone other than the speaker; read as the man speaking to his own father.
ph₂tréy: DAT of ph₂tḗr 'father' (or of peh₂tṓr 'protector').
kéh₃tum: ACC 'fight' as goal.
méǵh₂: neut NOM/ACC agreeing with ḱléwos; OPT unyéh₁s 'may you win'.

english: A snake was stealing the brothers' cattle and was hiding them in a dark hollow. They were seeking them and did not catch sight of them. Then they were coming to the grandson (nephew) and said to him: 'Grandson, seek the cattle for us (our cattle).' Then he grasped a spear and was following the path of those cattle. The path of hooves was drawing (leading) him to that hollow. That snake was lying in sleep, and she was sweating in the heat. Then she woke up and became restless. Then he struck her with that spear, and was killing the snake. Then the cattle came forth out of that hollow, and he was driving them to the men (or: was driving those men). They were giving him good fame. The grandson's name is famous (heard). He carried out that work successfully.
uncertain: h₂ewlóy / h₂ewlóm / h₂ewlṓd: 'something hollow, hollowed out'; cave presumably intended.
népotm̥ / népot / n̥ptés: 'grandson' (nephew/descendant possible).
nos: ACC/GEN/DAT.PL enclitic — 'seek the cattle for us' (DAT) or 'our cattle' (GEN).
gʷm̥yónt: PST 3PL 'were coming' (also a participle form).
stéygʰm̥: ACC.SG of steyks 'path' (analyzer also offers AOR 1SG 'I climbed', which does not fit).
tóm tóm h₂ewlóm: first tóm = 'him' (the grandson), second = 'that' with h₂ewlóm.
déwkt: PST 'was pulling/drawing' = led.
gʷʰéresi: LOC 'in the heat' (also SBJV/PRS 2SG verb forms, unlikely).
tónoh₁: INS of demonstrative 'with that' agreeing with ǵʰoysóh₁, or INS of tónos 'string'; chose demonstrative.
gʷʰént: PST 'was killing', not AOR 'killed'.
só-kʷe tóns wiHróns h₂éǵet: tóns wiHróns ACC.PL — goal 'drove [them] to the men' or object 'drove those men'; cattle not restated.
h₁wésu ḱléwos: neut NOM/ACC, read as object 'good fame'.
ḱlutóm: adj 'heard/famous' (analyzer also gives 2DU 'hear!').

english: A thirsty wolf saw a dog. It (the dog) was swollen (fat), and it was sitting. The wolf was saying to it: 'Who nourishes (feeds) you, dog?' It said: 'A man nourishes me, and I guard his sheep.' Then it (the wolf) caught sight of his (the man's) enclosure and said: 'You dwell in an enclosure. I dwell in the fields. I do not seek your enclosure.' Then it ran away. It was thirsty, and it was living (stayed alive). He who dwells in an enclosure is not a wolf.
uncertain: tr̥syónts / tr̥syét: 'thirsty' (hunger may have been intended in a wolf-and-dog fable).
tuh₂rós: derived adj from tewh₂- 'swell, grow fat'; no direct lexicon gloss — read 'fat'.
h₁ést: PST 'was' (also AOR of h₁es- 'throw', unlikely).
só tósyo gʰórtom kʷéḱt: só = the wolf (since the next speech is the wolf's); tósyo = the man's.
tḱéysi / tḱéymi / tḱéyti: 'settle, dwell' (also 'cultivate').
gʷíh₃wet: PST 'was living / was alive'.

english: A warrior was wearing bronze (copper), and was carrying around a spit/spear and a spear (javelin). He went to the fight and caught sight of guests (strangers). Looking at him, they were trembling. Then he struck a guest (stranger) and bored through him with that spit/spear. He fell, and death seized him. His bronze was red. He was sweating. Then they ran away. He was following them and was killing them. He was driving their cattle and horses, and gave the plunder to his father. The father said to him: 'Your fame will be imperishable, and your name will be famous.'
uncertain: gʷéru / gʷréwh₁: 'spit, skewer' / 'spear'; ǵʰoysóm 'spear, javelin' — two spear words.
gʰóstins / gʰóstim: lexicon gloss 'guest'; enemy/stranger presumably intended (hostis).
spéḱyontes: participle NOM.PL 'looking at'.
tónoh₁: INS demonstrative 'with that' (or tónos 'string' INS).
só séngʷt: 'he fell' = the struck guest, inferred.

tósyo h₂éyos h₁rudʰéh₁t: whose bronze is unclear — tósyo (non-reflexive) can mean the fallen guest's or the warrior's; read as the warrior's (stained). Also h₁rudʰéh₁t is PST 'was red' (stative), not 'became red'.
só swidyét: 'he was sweating' = the warrior, inferred.
tósyo ph₂tréy: 'his father' — the warrior's.
Hrowpóm: ACC of Hrowpós 'plunder, loot' (also a derived form glossed as emphatic).
h₁éseti: SBJV 'will be'.

english: The king was speaking to the young men: 'Whoever wins (overpowers), to him I will give bronze (copper).' Then they were yoking horses to the wheels (chariots), and drove to the stream. His (the king's) son was driving swift horses. He drove them on, and they ran. They were sweating. Then his wheel (chariot) was breaking (broke), and he fell from that wheel. A young warrior won. He was lifting his hands. Then the king was giving him bronze, and was saying to his son: 'Your horses are swift, and you will win bronze.'
uncertain: h₁yós wéneti tósmey: relative + SBJV 'whoever will win, to him'.
kʷékʷloybʰos / kʷékʷlos / kʷékʷlōd: 'wheel'; chariot presumably intended.
sréwmn̥: NOM/ACC; read ACC goal of h₁l̥h₂ént 'drove to the stream'.
tósyo suHnús: 'his son' — read as the king's son (only male antecedent).
Hrumptó: MID PST 3SG 'was breaking' (imperfective).
só tósyo ǵʰésorn̥s tl̥néh₂t: tósyo non-reflexive — 'his (someone else's) hands' or his own; read as his own. tl̥néh₂t PST 'was lifting'.
h₁opéyet: PST 'was giving' (gloss 'make reach; give').

wénesi: SBJV 2SG 'you will win' or exhortative 'may you win'. The prize-winning young warrior and the son who fell are different people; saying 'you will win bronze' to the son who fell reads oddly but is what the text says.

english: Darkness was thick, and the cattle of Dawn were lying in a hollow. That hollow was dark, and men did not catch sight of them. Those cattle were thirsty, and they grew tired. Then Dawn, daughter of the Sky, came to her brothers and said to them: 'Brothers, drive my cattle out of that hollow!' Then they were going to that hollow, and they split it. Then the cattle came forth, and the hollow grew bright (dawned). Their hooves shone. The sun was red, and the earth grew warm. The brothers were milking those cows and were sacrificing to Dawn. Dawn, giver of good things, protect us!
uncertain: h₂ewlós: 'something hollow'; cave presumably intended.
h₂usés: GEN/ABL/LOC of h₂éwsōs; read GEN 'of Dawn'.
tóns (twice): masc ACC.PL for the cattle.
tr̥syónt: PST 3PL 'were thirsty' (also participle).
tósyeh₂s bʰréh₂tern̥s: fem GEN 'her brothers'; ACC goal of gʷémt.
ih₂ént: PST 'were going (to)'.
sóh₂wl̥ h₁rudʰéh₁t: PST stative 'was red'.
h₂uséy: DAT of Dawn (analyzer also offers LOC of h₂ówsis 'light'); read 'to Dawn'.
h₂éwsos … déh₃tor: VOC; déh₃tor is the masculine agent noun 'giver' applied to a female deity.

english: A wolf was drinking at a full stream, and a yearling lamb was drinking. It (the lamb) saw the wolf and was trembling. Then it (the wolf) said to it: 'Lamb, you are drinking my water.' It said: 'I am not drinking it, and I am young.' It (the wolf) said: 'Your father was drinking it.' Then it seized it and ate it up. It is satisfied. The wolf does not listen to the lamb's word.
uncertain: pl̥h₁nóy: LOC.SG (or NOM/ACC.DU) agreeing with sruméni LOC.
wetsós: 'having a year' = yearling, modifying h₂egʷnós.
só tóm wĺ̥kʷom widét: só = the lamb (object is the wolf).
só tósmey wérh₁t: só = the wolf, inferred from the speech.
tetórpe: PRF 'is satisfied' (state).
ḱléwseti: PRS gnomic 'does not listen to'.

english: A king was seeking a son. Then he was sacrificing a horse and was burning it in fire. That fire licked it. Then Father Sky heard him and gave him a son. He grew, and he became a great warrior. He was stretching the bow. He was overcoming the father's guests (enemies) and was driving their cattle. The father rejoiced and said to him: 'By your fames (glories) it is great. May you be king.' Then he became king.
uncertain: h₁yáǵyet + ACC h₁éḱwom: 'was sacrificing a horse' (with DAT elsewhere = 'sacrifice to').
léyǵʰt: PST 'was licking'.
méǵh₂s-kʷe Hyudʰsmós bʰúHt: -kʷe on méǵh₂s starts the new clause: 'and he became a great warrior'; alternatively 'he grew great, and became a warrior'.
tn̥néwt / térh₂ut / h₂éǵet: PST imperfective forms, not AOR.
ph₂trés: GEN/ABL 'of the father' (also of peh₂tṓr 'protector'); not marked as 'his'.
gʰóstins: 'guests'; enemies presumably intended.
téwe ḱléwesbʰis méǵh₂ h₁ésti: ḱléwesbʰis is INS.PL 'with/by fames', méǵh₂ neut NOM/ACC 'great' with no neuter subject — does NOT say 'your fame is great' (that would be ḱléwos méǵh₂).
h₁syéh₁s: OPT 2SG 'may you be'.

english: The warriors arrived at a full river. It was big, and its waters were swift. They became afraid and did not find (see) a crossing. Then their king was sacrificing to that river and laid a horse in it. He said: 'River, goddess, giver of good things, give us a crossing!' Then it (the river) heard his word, and it was standing (still). Then they were walking (coming) on that crossing. They arrived at the field (pasture). He gave it (the river) a bull, and it was protecting him.
uncertain: pl̥h₁nóm déh₂nu: ACC goal of h₁ludʰónt (déh₂nu also NOM/LOC); pl̥h₁nóm thematic neut/masc ACC.
h₁ludʰónt: AOR 3PL 'arrived' (also participle).
tód / tósyo / tód-kʷe sth₂éh₁yet / tód-kʷe tóm h₂lékset: river referred to with neuter pronouns.
tósmey deh₂n̥wéy: DAT 'to that river'.
márkom: 'horse'; tósmi LOC 'in it'.
déh₂nu déywih₂ … déh₃tor: VOC; déywih₂ 'goddess' NOM/VOC; déh₃tor masc agent noun for a feminine addressee.
sth₂éh₁yet: PST 'was standing' — 'stood still' is an inference.
pr̥téwi: LOC 'on/in the crossing'.
só tósmey táwrom déh₃t: tósmey m/n DAT — read 'to it (the river)'; táwrom 'wild bull, aurochs'.
tód-kʷe tóm h₂lékset: PST 'it was protecting him' — the river protecting the king (or the bull?).

english: A bull — 'I ate' in the field — and he was sweating in the heat. A locust sat on his forehead and was speaking to him: 'Bull, I am big, and my wings are high. Do you not fear me? Shall I fly from your forehead?' The bull said: 'I do not fear you, and I did not see (notice) you. Sit on my forehead, or fly to that field.' Then the locust was flying to that field. It sat in it. The great ones did not see (do not notice) the locusts.
uncertain: h₁édm̥: AOR/PST 1SG 'I ate' — but the sentence has a 3rd-person subject (táwros); presumably 'was eating' (3SG) intended. Clause as written is ungrammatical.
gʷʰéresi: LOC 'in the heat' (also verb 2SG forms, unlikely).
h₂énti / h₂n̥tés: LOC/ABL of h₂ents 'forehead' (h₂énti also particle 'opposite, in front of'); 'horn' may have been intended.
bʰéh₂t: PST 'was speaking'.
bʰérǵʰonth₂: neut PL 'high' (adjective/participle).
bʰebʰóyh₂th₂e / bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e: PRF 'fear' (state).
pléwōh₂: SBJV 1SG of plew- 'fly, flow' — deliberative 'shall I fly'.
widóm: AOR 1SG 'I (did not) see/notice'.
pléwet: PST 'was flying'.
méǵh₂es … ne widónt: AOR 3PL (gnomic) 'the great did not / do not notice'; tóns sprongʰóns 'those locusts'.

english: A dog carrying meat came to a full river. It caught sight of that dog in the water which was carrying meat. It said: 'Let me seize (I will seize) that meat.' Then it entered that river, and its meat sank. It was swimming. It grew tired. The dog which it had seen vanished. Its meat is gone, and it went away from that river. He who carries meat, let him not look at that water.
uncertain: pl̥h₁nóm déh₂nu: ACC goal of gʷémt.
tóm ḱwónm̥ … h₁yós mḗms bʰéret: 'that dog which was carrying meat' — the reflection is never named as such.
gʰrébh₂oh₂: SBJV 1SG — 'I will / let me seize'.
tósyo mḗms: 'his meat' — non-reflexive tósyo; read as the dog's own meat.
snéh₂t: PST 'was swimming'.
néḱt: 'vanished, was lost'.
lelóykʷe: PRF 'is gone'.
léytt: AOR 'went away' (homonym léytt 'touched' unlikely).
mē spéḱyoyh₁t: prohibitive with OPT 'let him not look at'; tód wódr̥ ACC 'that water'.

english: A guest came to the king. He (the king) was seating him and was giving him meat and broth. He (the guest) ate that meat and was satisfied. He was sitting in the warmth. Then he (the king) said to him: 'What is your name?' He said: 'My name is famous (heard). I was killing the snake and was driving the cattle from the hollow.' Then he (the king) recognized (knew) him and rejoiced. He gave him his daughter and became his father-in-law. The father-in-law was giving horses to that son-in-law.
uncertain: sodéyet / h₁opéyet / sédyet: PST imperfective forms ('was seating, was giving, was sitting').
Subject switches (king vs guest) are not marked; assigned by sense.
tépesi: LOC of tépos 'heat, warmth' (also PRS 2SG of tep-, unlikely).
gʷʰénm̥ / h₂éǵom: PST 1SG 'I was killing / was driving', not AOR 'I killed'.
h₂ewlṓd: ABL 'from the hollow' (cave presumably intended).
ǵnéh₃t: AOR 'knew/recognized'.
tósyo dʰugh₂térm̥ / tósyo-kʷe swéḱuros: 'his daughter' = the king's own daughter (non-reflexive tósyo used reflexively), and 'his father-in-law' = the guest's.

english: The king's son was dwelling among guests (strangers). Then he went to his father's fields. His brothers were not recognizing him. His dog was lying in excrement/urine. It recognized him, and death took it. Then he came to his mother. She was saying: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am your son.' Then she was recognizing his word (voice), and she rejoiced. He was stretching the bow. Then he was killing the men who were devouring his cattle, and he became king. His fame is good.
uncertain: h₃réǵs: GEN/ABL 'of the king'.
gʰostéysu: LOC.PL 'among guests'.
ph₂trés: GEN 'of the father'; tósyo 'his'.
ǵn̥nh₃ént / ǵn̥néh₃t: PST 'were recognizing / was recognizing', vs ǵnéh₃t AOR 'recognized' for the dog.
múHtroy: LOC of múHtrom 'excrement, urine' (or NOM/ACC.DU); dung heap presumably intended.
só tóm ǵnéh₃t mértis-kʷe tóm sléh₂gʷt: só = the dog, tóm = the son; second tóm = the dog (taken by death) — could grammatically be the son.
wékʷos: 'word, speech'; 'voice' presumably intended.
gʷʰént: PST 'was killing'.
h₁yóy … gʷr̥h₃ónt: relative NOM.PL with PST 3PL 'were devouring' (form also a participle).
h₁wésu: neut 'good' with ḱléwos.

english: The wolves said to the sheep: 'Sheep, the dogs are guests (strangers/enemies) to you. Give them to us, and we will not eat you.' Those sheep were listening to their word, and (you two) were giving those dogs to them. Then they (the wolves) were killing them (the dogs), and came to them (the sheep). Those sheep were trembling and were speaking to them: 'Wolves, do not devour us!' They said: 'The dogs are gone; and who will protect you?' Then they were devouring them. They became sated. Whoever gives his dogs to the wolves, they eat him.
uncertain: h₂éwibʰos: DAT/ABL.PL; read DAT 'to the sheep'.
wos: ACC/GEN/DAT.PL enclitic 'you'; read DAT 'to you' (or GEN 'your guests').
gʰósteyes: 'guests'; enemies/strangers presumably intended.
h₁édomes: SBJV 1PL 'we will (not) eat'.
ḱléwsont: PST 3PL 'were listening' (or participle).
h₁opéyetom: PST/IMP 2DU 'you two gave / give!' — but the subject is 3PL 'those sheep'; presumably 3PL intended.
tóy tóns moréyont: tóy = wolves, tóns = dogs (both masc), inferred.
tā́s: fem ACC.PL = the sheep; gʷmént 'came to'.
mē gʷr̥h₃éte: prohibitive with PRS/PST 2PL form.
lelikʷḗr: PRF 3PL 'are gone'.
h₂léksēti: SBJV 3SG 'will protect'.
gʷr̥h₃ónt: PST 3PL 'were devouring' (or participle).
tósyo ḱwónn̥s: 'his dogs'; tóy tóm h₁dénti PRS 'they eat him'.

english: A sheep, on which there was no wool, has seen (saw) horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one (pulling) a great load, one carrying a man swiftly.
uncertain: owis, yāi, wl̥nā, eest, eḱwons, gʷr̥um, meǵm̥, ǵʰm̥onm̥, ōku: not in lexicon/analyzer (older Schleicher-style orthography); read from knowledge, not tool-verified.
yāi … ne eest: read as relative DAT/LOC fem 'on whom' + 'was not'.
dedorḱe: PRF 3SG 'has seen' (state/resultative rather than narrative past).
tom … tom … tom: ACC.SG demonstratives read distributively 'one … one … one' (horses).
tom bʰorom meǵm̥: no participle — verb 'pulling/carrying' supplied from context; bʰorom 'load, burden' ACC.
ǵʰm̥onm̥: read as ACC 'man (earthling)'; ōku 'swiftly'.

english: Man and Twin were dwelling (settling) in darkness. The earth was not, and the sky was not. Darkness was thick. Then Man said to Twin: 'Let us create the earth.' Twin said: 'Brother, sacrifice me!' Then he made him disappear (killed him), and was building the earth with his flesh, and was creating the sky with his forehead. He was creating the sun with his heat. Then he stood up on that earth and was setting up a place of sacrifice. He was placing fire in that place of sacrifice. That Twin became king of death, and his name is famous (heard). Those men are the grandsons (descendants) of Man.
uncertain: wiHrós / yemHós: 'man' / 'twin' used as names; no proper-name marking.
témHesi: LOC 'in darkness' (also SBJV 2SG 'grow faint', unlikely).
tḗtḱomes: SBJV 1PL 'let us create'.
h₁yáǵye: IMP 2SG 'sacrifice!' with me ACC 'me' (also VOC of an adjective, unlikely).
noḱéyet: PST 'was making disappear / causing death'.
démet / tḗtḱt / stoh₂éyet / stnéh₂t: all PST imperfective, not AOR.
mémsh₁ / h₂n̥téh₁ / gʷʰéresh₁: INS 'with/from his flesh / forehead / heat'.
sóh₂wl̥: NOM/ACC — read as object of tḗtḱt ('he created the sun'); could be subject ('the sun was creating [something] with his heat').
tósyeh₂i ǵʰémi: fem LOC 'on that earth'.
némos / némesi: 'bowing; sacrifice; place of sacrifice, clearing'.
mr̥téys: GEN 'of death' (not 'of the dead').
tóy wiHrṓs wiHrósyo népotes: 'those men' or 'men' (tóy as article); népotes 'grandsons'.

english: The Grandson of the Waters dwells in a full river. He is fire (Agni), and that river hides him. He burns in it. Who has seen him? Men have not seen him. Then they were seeking fire and went to the stream. They were saying to that stream: 'Stream, give us fire!' Then it gave them that Grandson, and he was warming them, and they were sweating. They were cooking meat, and ate it, and were satisfied. They were sacrificing to him. The Grandson is the giver of good things. 'Grandson of the Waters, give us good things!'
uncertain: wédnōm népōts: GEN.PL 'of the waters' + 'grandson'.
pl̥h₁nóy déh₂n̥wi: LOC (pl̥h₁nóy also NOM/ACC.DU).
tód-kʷe déh₂nu tóm ḱéleti: neuter tód with déh₂nu; ḱéleti PRS 'hides' (or SBJV of ḱel-).
dedórḱe / dedr̥ḱḗr: PRF 'has seen / have seen'.
sréwmn̥-kʷe gʷh₂ént: ACC goal.
dédh₃dʰi: IMP of reduplicated present 'keep giving / give'.
nu tód tóybʰos tóm népotm̥ h₁opéyet: tód = the stream (neut NOM); h₁opéyet PST 'was giving / made reach'.
tr̥pént: AOR of terp- 'were satisfied' (analyzer also offers trep- 'turned').
h₁yáǵyont + DAT: 'were sacrificing to'.
h₁wésuh₂: neut NOM/ACC.PL 'good things'.

english: A sheep standing by the stream saw horses. They were pulling a big wheel (chariot) and were carrying a man. That sheep said to them: 'Horses, the man pulls you, and you carry him. Do you not fear him?' They said: 'Listen, sheep! We do not fear him. He gives us water, and he cooks your flesh.' Then the sheep, hearing that, ran away to the field. He who knows (has seen) the man fears him.
uncertain: sth₂éh₁yontih₂: fem participle NOM.SG 'standing' with h₂ówis.
kʷékʷlom: 'wheel'; chariot/cart presumably intended.
duként / wéǵʰont: PST 3PL 'were pulling / were carrying'.
h₁éḱwōs só wiHrós usmé déwkti: VOC h₁éḱwōs then NOM só wiHrós; usmé ACC.PL 'you'.
wéǵʰete: PRS/PST/IMP 2PL — read PRS 'you carry' (IMP 'carry him!' possible).
bʰebʰih₂é / bʰebʰih₂mé / bʰebʰóyh₂e: PRF 'fear' (state); final bʰebʰóyh₂e is 1SG or 3SG, read 3SG.
téwe-kʷe mḗms pékʷeti: téwe GEN 'your (sg.) flesh/meat' — i.e. the sheep's.
ḱléwsontih₂: fem participle 'hearing/listening'.
h₂éǵrom dréh₂t: ACC goal 'ran (away) to the field'.
wóyde: PRF 'has seen, knows'.

english: 'Let it be,' said the bright god Werunos.
uncertain: wérunos: not in lexicon/analyzer — taken as a divine name (cf. Varuna/Ouranos).
wéwked: spelled with final -d (analyzer maps to wéwket AOR 3SG 'said').
h₁estu: IMP 3SG 'let it be' (also IMP of h₁es- 'throw', unlikely).
lewkós deywós: NOM 'bright god' in apposition to Werunos.

english: The Twins drive swift horses. Their horses fly, and their wheel (chariot) is swift. Dawn, daughter of the Sky, is their sister. A lamb fell (sank) in a dark stream and said to them: 'Twins, protect me! Death is devouring me.' Then they heard his word and drove to him. Then they were lifting him and were seating him on that wheel (chariot). He grew cold, and they were warming him. He rejoiced and said to those twins: 'Your fame is great. May your name be famous.'
uncertain: yemHṓs / yemHóybʰos: plural, not dual — 'the twins' as a plural group.
h₂éǵonti: PRS 3PL 'drive' (or SBJV of h₂eǵ- 'say', unlikely).
pléwonti: PRS 3PL of plew- 'fly, flow, run'.
kʷékʷlos / kʷékʷloy: 'wheel'; chariot presumably intended.
séngʷt: AOR 'fell / sank / went under'.
Hreh₁móy sruméni: LOC 'in a dark stream'.
h₂léksete: IMP 2PL 'protect!'.
tóm-kʷe h₁l̥h₂ént: ACC goal 'drove to him'.
tl̥nh₂ént / sodéyont / gʷʰr̥nwént: PST imperfective.
só stéwdt: AOR 'became cold'.
wos: 2PL enclitic GEN 'your'.
h₁syéh₁t: OPT 'may it be'.

english: The king was speaking to the warriors: 'Warriors, listen to my word. Guests (strangers/enemies) have reached our fields and are stealing our cattle. Seize spits/spears and yoke horses to the wheels (chariots)! Let us overcome them. Let us go to them and make them disappear (kill them). Whoever falls in the fight, his fame will be imperishable. Whoever runs away, dogs will eat him.' Then they heard the word of that king and ran to them.
uncertain: ḱléwsete: PRS/PST/IMP 2PL — read IMP 'listen!'.
nos: ACC/GEN/DAT enclitic — read GEN 'our' both times.
gʰósteyes: 'guests'; enemies presumably intended.
h₂eh₂n̥ḱḗr: PRF 3PL 'have reached'.
gʷéruh₂: 'spits, skewers / spears' NOM/ACC.PL.
yungté: PRS/PST/IMP 2PL — read IMP.
térh₂womes / gʷéh₂omes / noḱéyōmes: SBJV 1PL 'let us'.
kh₃téwi: LOC 'in the fight'.
séngʷeti / dréh₂eti / h₁édonti / h₁éseti: SBJV (future/general).
tósyo h₃réǵs: GEN 'of that king'.
tóns-kʷe dr̥mént: ACC.PL goal 'ran to them' (the guests/enemies).

english: The mother, a goddess, said to her son: 'If you go to the fight, death will grasp you, and your fame will be imperishable. If you sit at your father's fire, you will see your grandsons, and your name will not be famous.' Then he said: 'Mother, I will go to that fight. May death take me, and may my fame be imperishable.' Then he was yoking horses to a new wheel (chariot), and drove to that fight. His horses were flying. She was watching him and was trembling. She is mindful of (remembers) his name.
uncertain: méh₂tēr déywih₂: both NOM — 'the mother, a goddess' (or 'the goddess mother').
suHnówey: DAT 'to the son' — no possessive.
h₁yód + SBJV (gʷéh₂esi, sísdēsi, widḗsi): 'if you go / sit / see'; kapyḗti, h₁éseti SBJV future.
kapyḗti: SBJV of kap- 'grasp'.
ph₂trés: GEN 'of the father' (also of peh₂tṓr 'protector'); ph₂wéni LOC 'at the fire'.
gʷéh₂oh₂: SBJV 1SG 'I will go'.
sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t / h₁syéh₁t: OPT 'may … take / be'.
néwōy kʷékʷlōy: DAT 'to a new wheel'.
yunégt: PST 'was yoking'; pléwont PST 3PL 'were flying/running'.
séh₂ (twice): 'she' = the mother, inferred.
memóne: PRF 3SG 'is mindful of, remembers' (state).
